title: Decaf Coffee, Pre-sweetened with Low Calorie Sweetener

content.title: About
content.content: Decaf coffee pre‑sweetened with a low‑calorie sweetener is a beverage made from roasted coffee beans that have had most of the caffeine removed, then blended with a low‑calorie sweetener. It retains the characteristic flavor notes of regular coffee without the stimulating effect.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Decaffeination can be performed by solvent, water, or super‑critical CO₂ methods.
Low‑calorie sweeteners such as stevia or erythritol provide sweetness without added sugar.
Decaf coffee is often chosen for evening consumption to avoid sleep disturbances.
Antioxidant levels in decaf coffee are nearly identical to those in regular coffee.
In some countries decaf coffee is considered a safer option for people with high blood pressure.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Coffee antioxidants help protect blood vessels from oxidative stress.

items.title: Promotes liver function
items.content: Studies suggest regular coffee consumption, including decaf, may benefit liver health.

items.title: Helps regulate blood sugar
items.content: Low‑calorie sweeteners do not cause rapid glucose spikes.

items.title: May reduce risk of type 2 diabetes
items.content: Decaf coffee can improve insulin sensitivity.

items.title: Improves mood without stimulation
items.content: The aroma and flavor of coffee can have a calming effect without caffeine’s stimulant properties.

items.title: Coffee allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to coffee components.

items.title: Sweetener tolerance
items.content: Some low‑calorie sweeteners may cause gastrointestinal discomfort in large amounts.

items.title: Decaffeination method residues
items.content: Solvent‑based processes can leave trace residues if not properly removed.

items.title: Bone health considerations
items.content: Excessive coffee intake, even decaf, may increase calcium excretion.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Prepare decaf coffee like regular coffee: use 1‑2 tsp of ground coffee per 180 ml of water at 90‑95 °C, steep for 3‑5 minutes, then filter. Add milk, plant‑based milks, or spices to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the package in a cool, dry place away from direct light. After opening, keep in an airtight container and use within 2‑3 weeks.
